label: TP
reason: User-supplied HTTP header names flow directly into the HTML response via ESAPI.encodeForHTML(), which encodes the header NAME but ignores the HEADER VALUE used for hashing. Since the actual sensitive payload (the header VALUE) is written unencoded to the response, an attacker can inject arbitrary characters including '<script>' tags into the displayed content, resulting in a reflected XSS vulnerability.

evidence.note: param is assigned the header NAME from getHeaders(), bypassing any validation of the header VALUE.
The header VALUE (from bar.getBytes()) is converted to bytes and passed to MessageDigest, losing control over what gets encoded.
Response prints the decoded String(input) which contains the original unfiltered header VALUE, allowing XSS payloads to reflect.
